title: Eliezer Ben-Yehuda established a home that spoke only Hebrew and compiled a dictionary that was completed in 17 volumes

trailer.text: Eliezer Ben-Yehuda was a Hebrew writer and lexicographer, and according to the Encyclopaedia Judaica he is generally considered the father of modern Hebrew.
He was born in 1858 in Lithuania, the son of a Chabad Hasid, and studied at a yeshiva.
In October 1881 he arrived with his wife in Jaffa, and there he informed her that henceforth they would speak to each other only in Hebrew.
According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, their home was the first Hebrew-speaking home in the Land of Israel.
When he arrived in the Land of Israel he began collecting material for a modern Hebrew dictionary, and the dictionary was completed in 1959, in 17 volumes.

stations.title: A Boy from Lithuania and a Language That Was Not Spoken

paragraphs.text: Eliezer Ben-Yehuda was born Eliezer Perelman in Luzhky, Lithuania, in 1858.
According to Maariv, his father died when he was 5.
He was the son of a Chabad Hasid and was given a traditional religious education at a local yeshiva.
In 1878 he went to Paris to study medicine, so that he would have a profession to support himself in the Land of Israel.
In the "Great Introduction" he wrote that in Paris he had difficulty conducting conversations in Hebrew with his acquaintances, because many words were lacking.
In the winter of 1878 he contracted tuberculosis, and so he decided to discontinue his studies and settle in the more favorable climate of the Land of Israel.
He saw Jewish nationalism as two things together: a return to the homeland and a revival of Hebrew.
According to MyJewishLearning, for centuries Hebrew was used only in study, and not as a spoken language.
In Jerusalem, Jews spoke Yiddish, French or Arabic in everyday life.
According to Maariv, Ben-Yehuda and Devora Jonas met in Vienna, continued to Cairo, where they married, and from there immigrated to the Land of Israel.
In October 1881 they arrived in Jaffa, and there he informed her that henceforth they would speak to each other only in Hebrew.
In 1882 their son Ben-Zion was born.
According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, the family was the first Hebrew-speaking home in the Land of Israel, and Ben-Zion, later Ithamar Ben-Avi, was the first child of modern times to speak Hebrew.
According to Maariv, Devora died of tuberculosis.
A year after her death her sister Beila, Hemda, came to the Land of Israel and married Ben-Yehuda that same year.

stations.title: A newspaper, a school and Va'ad ha-Lashon

paragraphs.text: As early as 1881, Ben-Yehuda founded, together with others, the society “Te?iyyat Israel”.
He taught at the Alliance school in Jerusalem, only after he was permitted to teach all Jewish subjects in Hebrew alone.
In 1884 Ben-Yehuda began work on the newspaper Ha-Zevi.
According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, his newspaper was the first Hebrew newspaper to meet European standards, despite its defects.
In 1890, together with David Yellin, Aaron Masie and others, he founded Va'ad ha-Lashon, and presided over it until his death.
According to Dr. Reuven Gafni, the committee became a significant body and in time became the Academy of the Hebrew Language.
He gained the support of nationalist educators who identified with his project.
According to Dr. Neta Dan, he did not found most of the Hebrew educational institutions himself, but their founders drew inspiration from his energy and his vision.
According to Maariv, during the Second Aliyah, 1904–1914, Hebrew began to be commonly spoken in kindergartens and schools, especially in the moshavot.
By his own account, what first drove him to work on the dictionary was the pressing need to speak in Hebrew.
When he arrived in the Land of Israel he began collecting material, and at times worked 18 hours a day developing new words and writing articles.
According to Zohar Shavit, the first plan was a pocket dictionary.
Later it grew into a dictionary in three or four volumes, and finally into a historical-scientific dictionary.
In a letter from 1906 Ben-Yehuda wrote that without an assistant and in great hardship he had himself copied enormous quantities of material, and that he had half a million index cards.
According to Maariv, he had to coin words that did not exist in the Hebrew of the Bible and the Mishnah.
According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, he was the first to coin Hebrew words in a regular and systematic way.
Among his coinages, according to the sources: sidewalk, brush, train, omelet, police, emigration, identity, doll, ice cream, towel and bicycle.
According to the academic article, Ben-Yehuda sought support from Zionist institutions, and received from them neither support nor encouragement.
With no choice, he turned to non-Zionist institutions, chief among them Kol Yisrael Haverim, the Alliance.
They agreed to provide support on condition that senior scholars give their opinion, and the scholars determined that the dictionary should be historical-scientific.
Ben-Yehuda and his wife approached the scholars Goldziher, Bacher, Dalman and Blau, and according to the academic article they enthusiastically confirmed the scientific value of the dictionary.
On October 4, 1897 he received a loan of 5,000 francs from Kol Yisrael Haverim, a hundred times his monthly salary as a teacher.
According to Maariv, he also received a regular stipend from Baron Rothschild and in effect became the Baron's employee.
The first volume was dedicated to the Baron, who contributed to the work for many years.
In 1910 he began to publish the dictionary volume by volume, assisted by various sponsors.
The First World War disrupted the plans, and the couple again had to look for donors.
In his lifetime he saw five volumes.
After his death his widow and his son Ehud continued, and the dictionary was completed in 1959, in 17 volumes.
According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, Ben-Yehuda and Ussishkin persuaded the High Commissioner Herbert Samuel to declare Hebrew one of the three official languages of the country.
According to Aish, the British Mandate government recognized Hebrew as one of the three official languages.
According to Maariv, Ben-Yehuda died at his home on a Saturday, and Ahad Ha'am sent words of condolence to the family.
According to Arutz 7, about 35% of the members of the Jewish Yishuv in the Land at that time took part in the funeral.
Ahad Ha'am sent words of condolence to the family, and wrote that the enterprise to which Ben-Yehuda had dedicated his life would be a monument of honor to him among his people forever.
Two days after his death Mordechai Ben-Hillel wrote in Haaretz that his name would be raised high as one of the heroes of the Israelite nation.
The British historian Cecil Roth said, according to Aish, that before Ben-Yehuda Jews could speak Hebrew, and after him they did speak it.
The Knesset designated his birthday, the twenty-first of Tevet, as Hebrew Language Day.
According to MyJewishLearning, Ben-Yehuda took extreme measures, and tried to prevent his son from playing with other children and from hearing other languages.
According to Devorah Omer's book, as cited in Maariv, his wife was forbidden to bring friends for the child, even though her mother tongue was Yiddish and Russian.
According to Arutz 7, until age 3 Itamar did not speak, and some claimed that the experiment was not working.
According to Dr. Neta Dan, in his first years in the Land of Israel he was met with suspicion and doubt.
At first he adopted the customs of the Orthodox in order to get closer to them, but they suspected him, and he became an extremist in his antireligious position.
According to Dr. Gafni, he came out against the Old Yishuv and against the halukka funds.
According to Maariv, in his articles he attacked the Perushim of the kollel, and they boycotted him.
According to Arutz 7, the Chevra Kadisha opposed burying him on the Mount of Olives, until Rabbi Yitzhak Arieli permitted the burial.
In the Hanukkah issue of Ha-Zevi he published an article by his father-in-law Jonas, which called for joining forces and reviving the honor of the nation.
After he was informed on to the Turkish authorities he was declared a "rebel against the kingdom", and was sentenced to a year in prison.
Ten days later he was released, and under pressure from the Baron and public figures a retrial was held.
After the Turkish censorship was tightened, he concentrated more on linguistic questions.
According to Zohar Shavit, most Zionist bodies showed lack of interest, indifference and even hostility toward the dictionary, and Hayim Nahman Bialik, more than anyone, set this attitude.
According to Dr. Gafni, Bialik and Agnon criticized Ben-Yehuda for being "a factory of words".
Agnon claimed in "Kenagen ha-Menagen" that Ben-Yehuda invented nothing.
According to Prof. Zuckermann, Ben-Yehuda and his followers did not succeed in freeing Hebrew from the shackles of Yiddish.

disagreements.question: In what year was the Hanukkah article published?

versions.says: Encyclopaedia Judaica: in the 1894 Hanukkah issue

disagreements.question: Did he found Ha-Zevi or edit an existing newspaper?

versions.says: Maariv: in October 1884 he began editing Ha-Zevi, which operated under the license of Rabbi Haim Hirschensohn
Encyclopaedia Judaica: at the end of 1884 he founded the weekly Ha-Zevi, which became the biweekly Ha-Or

disagreements.question: When did Devora die, and when did he marry Hemda?

versions.says: Maariv: Devora died in 1890, and Hemda married him a year later
Encyclopaedia Judaica: his wife died in 1891, and he married her sister about six months later

disagreements.question: When was Hebrew declared an official language?

versions.says: Maariv: on his return to Jerusalem in 1919 he was among those who influenced Herbert Samuel
Aish: in 1922 the Mandate government recognized it

disagreements.question: How many words did he coin?

versions.says: Dr. Neta Dan of the Academy of the Hebrew Language: about 220

claims.text: לפי המאמר האקדמי, כשהגה בן-יהודה את המילון השימושי ניסה לקבל תמיכה ממוסדות ציוניים אך לא קיבל מהם תמיכה ולא עידוד.
claims.quote: כבר כשהגה את הרעיון לחבר מילון שימושי ניסה בן יהודה לזכות בתמיכה מצד כמה מוסדות ציוניים אך לא קיבל מהם לא תמיכה ולא עידוד.

claims.text: לפי המאמר האקדמי, בן-יהודה פנה בלית ברירה למוסדות לא ציוניים, ובראשם חברת כי"ח (אליאנס).
claims.quote: בצר לו פנה לכמה מוסדות לא ציוניים, ובראשם לחברת כי"ח.

claims.text: לפי המאמר האקדמי, המוסדות הלא ציוניים הסכימו לתמוך בתנאי שמלומדים בכירים יחוו דעה, והמלומדים קבעו שהמילון צריך להיות היסטורי-מדעי.
claims.quote: אלה היו נכונים לתמוך במילון בתנאי שמלומדים מן השורה הראשונה יחוו דעתם על המילון, והמלומדים האלה קבעו שעל המילון להיות מילון היסטורי־מדעי.

claims.text: לפי המאמר האקדמי, בן-יהודה ורעייתו פנו לחוקרים בכירים (גולדציהר, בכר, דלמן ובלאו), והם אישרו בהתלהבות את הערך המדעי של המילון.
claims.quote: ואכן, בן יהודה ורעייתו פנו לשורה של חוקרים מהשורה הראשונה, ובהם הפרופסורים גולדציהר, בכר, דלמן ובלאו, שאישרו בהתלהבות את ערכו המדעי של המילון.

claims.text: לפי המאמר האקדמי, ב-4 באוקטובר 1897 קיבל בן-יהודה מכי"ח הלוואה חריגה של 5,000 פרנק, פי מאה ממשכורתו החודשית כמורה בבית ספר של כי"ח.

claims.text: לפי מעריב, בן-יהודה קיבל קצבה קבועה מהברון רוטשילד והפך למעשה לפקיד הברון.

claims.quote: To ingratiate himself with the Orthodox Jews who knew written Hebrew and could, therefore, readily learn to speak the language, Ben Yehuda at first adopted their customs.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיה יודאיקה, האורתודוקסים חשדו בו, ובן-יהודה הפך לקיצוני בעמדתו האנטי-דתית.
claims.quote: They began to suspect him, and Ben-Yehuda became an extremist in his antireligious attitude.

claims.quote: הוא יצא נגד היישוב הישן ונגד כספי החלוקה, כלומר כספי הצדקה שהקהילות האשכנזיות היו מושתתות עליהם

claims.text: לפי מעריב, בן-יהודה תקף במאמריו את אנשי הכולל הפרושים והוחרם על ידם.
claims.quote: במאמריו, הוא הצליף באנשי הכולל הפרושים ובתגובה הוחרם על ידיהם.

claims.text: לפי מעריב, בחנוכה תרנ"ד (1893) פרסם בן-יהודה בהצבי מאמר שכתב חותנו יונאס, שקרא לאיחוד כוחות ולהחייאת כבוד העם.
claims.quote: בחנוכה תרנ"ד 1893 פרסם בן־יהודה ב"הצבי" מאמר שכתב חותנו יונאס, שבו קרא לאיחוד כוחות ולהחייאת כבוד העם.

claims.text: לפי מעריב, בן-יהודה הוכרז "מורד מלכות" בעקבות הלשנה לשלטונות הטורקיים, רבני העדות הסירו אחריות מהמאמר, והוא נשפט ונידון לשנת מאסר.
claims.quote: בן־יהודה הוכרז כ"מורד מלכות", רבני העדות הספרדית והאשכנזית הסירו את אחריותם מהמאמר, והוא נשפט ונידון למאסר למשך שנה.

claims.text: לפי מעריב, בן-יהודה שוחרר כעבור עשרה ימים, ובלחץ הברון ואנשי ציבור נערך משפט חוזר.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיה יודאיקה, בעקבות החמרת הצנזורה הטורקית על הצבי התרכז בן-יהודה יותר בשאלות לשון שהצנזורים לא יכלו להתנגד להן.
claims.quote: As a result, Ben-Yehuda began to concentrate more on linguistic questions to which the censors could make no objection.

claims.text: לפי זהר שביט, רוב הגופים הציוניים גילו חוסר עניין, אדישות ואף עוינות כלפי מפעל המילון ההיסטורי של בן-יהודה.

claims.text: לפי זהר שביט, חיים נחמן ביאליק היה מי שקבע יותר מכל את היחס הקריר, האדיש ואף העוין של ההנהגה הציונית למפעלו של בן-יהודה.
claims.quote: מי שקבע יותר מכול את ההתייחסות הקרירה, האדישה ואפילו העוינת של ההנהגה למפעלו של בן־יהודה, היה חיים נחמן ביאליק.

claims.quote: היו אנשי לשון וספרות שביקרו אותו - ביאליק, עגנון, על כך שהוא בית חרושת של מילים.

claims.text: לפי ד"ר גפני, עגנון מתח ב"כנגן המנגן" ביקורת חריפה על מיתוס בן-יהודה וטען שלא המציא דבר.
claims.quote: ב'כנגן המנגן' עגנון מתח ביקורת חריפה מאוד על מיתוס בן־יהודה, וטען שלא המציא דבר.
